mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 4% for two consecutive months predicts higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to expectations of future rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains >4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS accompanied by UNRATE below 5% suggests a tight labor market without wage inflation, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month while UNRATE < 5%
regime_hint: labor market tightening without wage pressures
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under this signal are negative and remain so across 5 consecutive windows.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST and RSAFS above 1100 and 450,000 respectively signals robust industrial and consumer demand, predicting positive S&P 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1100 and RSAFS > 450,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when both proxies are above thresholds for at least 3 months in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO below 105 indicates softening manufacturing capacity, which tends to depress equities and predict negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during INDPRO < 105 periods.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL accelerating at a monthly rate above 0.3% for three months predicts a disinflationary shift and higher S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate > 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under this signal are flat or negative over 10 such windows.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE falling below 4% for two consecutive months in a context of rising PAYEMS suggests a labor market shift favoring equities, predicting positive 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months and PAYEMS increasing
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive when UNRATE remains below 4% for >4 months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in GDPC1 of over 2% indicate weakening demand absorption, which tends to depress equities and produce negative S&P 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during GDPC1 declines >2% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three consecutive months in a non-inflationary macro context predicts negative S&P 60-day forward returns due to higher real rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 250
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not negative when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months without a subsequent CPIAUCSL decline.
